children: The U.S. Treasury auction of 30-year bonds Thursday showed slightly softer- than-expected demand.
The Treasury sold $25 billion in bonds at its monthly auction, with a high yield of 5.441%. The high yield compared with a market yield of 5.437% at the time.
Following the auction, the 30-year yield rose to 5.447%.
Indirect bidders, a group that includes foreign institutional buyers, acquired 68% of competitive awards, compared to 72% at the last auction.
The bid-to-cover ratio, a measure of investor demand, was 2.36, compared with 2.54 in October.
